config.title: contain and content-visibility

intro.title: contain and content-visibility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a webpage with multiple sections to learn how to optimize rendering performance using CSS containment properties. You will explore the 'contain' property to isolate parts of your layout and the 'content-visibility' property to skip rendering off-screen content. The core concept involves using these CSS declarations to improve page load speed and scrolling smoothness by controlling how the browser processes elements. You will work directly with CSS in a stylesheet, applying these properties to div elements to see their practical effects. By the end, you will understand how to implement these techniques to create more efficient web pages.
intro.usecase: The contain and content-visibility properties are essential for optimizing complex web interfaces like data dashboards and e-commerce product grids. When developers build analytics dashboards with multiple interactive charts and tables, these CSS properties prevent layout thrashing during user interactions like filtering or sorting. In e-commerce sites with infinite-scrolling product listings, content-visibility dramatically improves initial page load by deferring rendering of off-screen items. These optimizations are crucial for maintaining smooth 60fps performance in content-heavy applications where users expect responsive interactions.

Configure content-visibility to optimize rendering performance for off-screen content

steps.title: Create the HTML structure for the demonstration
steps.instruction: Create a basic HTML structure with a main container, several content sections, and nested elements that will be styled with CSS containment and content-visibility properties.
steps.hint: Start with a div element with class 'demo-container'. Inside it, create multiple sections with different content types like text, images, and nested divs.

successCriteria: HTML structure includes a main container with multiple content sections containing nested elements
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You have some HTML structure, but make sure you have a main container with multiple sections containing nested content.

steps.title: Add base styles for layout and visibility
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to create a grid layout for the .demo-container, give each .section a border, padding, and background color, and style the .nested-content elements.
steps.hint: Use display: grid for the container, and apply properties like border, padding, and background to make the sections visually distinct.
steps.expectedOutcome: The demonstration will have a grid layout with clearly visible sections, making it easier to observe the effects of contain and content-visibility in later steps.
successCriteria: CSS includes grid layout for .demo-container, and each .section has border, padding, and background color applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure all required styles (grid, border, padding, background) are applied correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The base styles are missing or incomplete. Review the instruction to add grid layout and section styling.

steps.title: Introduce the contain property with 'layout' value
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property `contain: layout;` to the `.demo-container` class to establish layout containment.
steps.hint: Look for the `.demo-container` selector in your CSS and add the `contain` property with the value `layout`.
steps.expectedOutcome: The `.demo-container` element will have layout containment applied, creating a formatting context that isolates its layout from the rest of the page.
successCriteria: The `.demo-container` selector includes the property `contain: layout;`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added `contain: layout;` to the `.demo-container` selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The `.demo-container` selector should include `contain: layout;`. Try adding that property.

steps.title: Apply contain: paint to hide overflow
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for the .section class that sets contain: paint; to create paint containment.
steps.hint: Paint containment establishes a stacking context and clips content at the element's bounds. Add the rule after the existing .demo-container rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .section elements will have paint containment applied, creating stacking contexts and clipping overflow content.
successCriteria: The .section class has a CSS rule with contain: paint; property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're adding contain: paint; to the .section class selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add a CSS rule for .section with contain: paint; to establish paint containment.

steps.title: Combine contain values with 'strict'
steps.instruction: In your CSS, add a new rule for the class .strict-section and apply the shorthand contain: strict; to it.
steps.hint: The 'strict' value is a shorthand that combines layout, paint, and style containment. It provides maximum isolation for the element from the rest of the document.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for .strict-section is created with contain: strict; applied.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .strict-section selector with the property contain set to strict.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created a rule for .strict-section and set contain to strict.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding a CSS rule for .strict-section with contain: strict;. Please try again.

steps.title: Use contain: content for balanced containment
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a class named .content-section and apply contain: content; to it.
steps.hint: The contain: content; value provides layout and paint containment but allows styles to affect descendants.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule with contain: content; is created for the .content-section class.
successCriteria: The .content-section rule exists with contain: content; applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a rule for .content-section and applied contain: content; to it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .content-section with contain: content; wasn't found. Try adding it as shown in the example.

steps.title: Introduce content-visibility: auto for performance
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for the .auto-section class that applies content-visibility: auto to enable browser optimization for off-screen content.
steps.hint: Use the content-visibility property with the value 'auto' to allow the browser to skip rendering content outside the viewport.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .auto-section will have content-visibility: auto applied, enabling performance optimization by skipping rendering of off-screen content.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for .auto-section exists and includes content-visibility: auto.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a rule for .auto-section with content-visibility: auto.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding a CSS rule for .auto-section with content-visibility: auto. Check your syntax and try again.

steps.title: Use content-visibility: hidden to hide content
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for the class .hidden-section to apply content-visibility: hidden;
steps.hint: Create a new selector .hidden-section and set the content-visibility property to hidden.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .hidden-section elements will be removed from rendering but maintain their layout size and position.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for .hidden-section with content-visibility: hidden; is added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the .hidden-section selector with content-visibility: hidden;.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .hidden-section with content-visibility: hidden; is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Combine contain and content-visibility for optimal performance
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS rule for the class .combined-section that applies both contain: strict and content-visibility: auto to maximize rendering performance.
steps.hint: Add a new selector .combined-section with both properties in the same rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for .combined-section that includes both contain: strict and content-visibility: auto properties.
successCriteria: The .combined-section selector exists with both contain: strict and content-visibility: auto properties correctly applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your .combined-section rule includes both contain: strict and content-visibility: auto properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .combined-section rule is missing or doesn't have the required properties. Try adding both contain: strict and content-visibility: auto.

steps.title: Create a practical example with scrollable content
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a .scrollable-container class that creates a scrollable area with multiple items, applying contain: content and content-visibility: auto to optimize rendering performance during scrolling.
steps.hint: Define the .scrollable-container class with fixed dimensions, overflow-y: auto to enable vertical scrolling, and apply both contain: content and content-visibility: auto properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for .scrollable-container is added with contain: content and content-visibility: auto properties to demonstrate performance optimization in a real-world scrollable scenario.
successCriteria: The .scrollable-container rule includes contain: content, content-visibility: auto, overflow-y: auto, and appropriate dimensions for scrolling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your .scrollable-container rule includes both contain: content and content-visibility: auto properties, along with overflow-y: auto for scrolling functionality.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .scrollable-container rule is missing key properties. It should include contain: content, content-visibility: auto, overflow-y: auto, and appropriate dimensions to create a functional scrollable container with performance optimizations.
